evals.prompt: Our wordmark sits in a box 2300 wide by 1400 tall with the letters 910 tall and 120 margins top and bottom. Can you check whether the proportions are balanced and tell me what to move, without changing the lean of the box?
evals.expected_output: A measurement table from proportion_check with verdicts, the letter block and margins compared with 0.618 / 0.382 of the box height, a short list of nudges with the values, the lean left alone, and a note that the grid should be drawn on a locked layer with the values recorded.

evals.prompt: I'm setting up the type for a new site in Figma, body 17px, and I need heading sizes, line heights and a spacing scale that feel like one system. Give me the values I can type into variables.
evals.expected_output: The type rule from body 17: every level as a ratio of body, whole steps only (small 0.618, body 1, subhead 1.618, heading 2 2.618, heading 1 4.236, display 6.854), with px as a calculated column (11, 17, 28, 45, 72, 117) from golden_grid.py scale --body 17; no half steps unless the contract turns them on; line heights 1.618 / 1.272 / 1.0; the spacing sequence 8 13 21 34 55 89; the typeface and body recorded as a version with golden_grid.py version; and the Figma route: the plugin's Golden variables with type/body as the one number to edit, or CSS tokens from golden_grid.py scale --body 17 --format css.

evals.prompt: The landing page hero feels off. Desktop is 1440 wide. Where should the headline and the product shot go and how wide should the text column be?
evals.expected_output: Hero as a 1440 by 890 golden rectangle, the eye at about (1042, 644), phi lines at 550 and 890, text column 0.618 of the inner width, product shot on the eye or a crossing, with the page grid SVG offered.

evals.prompt: Our wordmark is cut out of a box and the outer proportions now check out, but it still feels busy. Measured at full size: stems 82.8, horizontals 94.9 after a 1.3 vertical stretch of our own font (stem 220 and horizontal 194 font units), letter gaps 29.8 next to round letters and 33.1 between straight ones, slits 29.4 and 29.9, e crossbar 43.1, counters 50.0 to 52.3 wide, box line 15.45. What should change so every shape and weight holds together?
evals.expected_output: A --ladder report on the stem with 2 of 8 on; horizontals 1.146 of the stems; a stretch of 1.134 (220 / 194) makes horizontals equal the stems; counters already within 3 percent of s/phi and kept; a proposed ladder of 19.55, 31.6, 51.2 and 82.8 with each part assigned a step (line s/phi^3, gaps and crossbar s/phi^2, counters s/phi, stems s); round-side gaps at 0.9 of the gap logged as an optical departure; the chance rate stated so single hits are not oversold.

evals.prompt: Here is our lockup exported from Illustrator as outlines: a brain icon drawn as one line with folds, and the wordmark in General Sans Semibold beside it (lockup.svg). Before we export the final files, check that every part holds together: the icon's line weight and the gaps between its folds, the wordmark's stem and x-height, and the space between the icon and the word. Don't measure it by hand.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/logo_measure.py on the SVG with python3 -I and a quoted path, without hand measurements. Reports each shape's line width (median, p10, p90, min, max, uneven flag), the fold gaps (median, p10, p90, min, max and where the narrowest are), counters, the two parts and the gap between them, and for the word the baseline, x-height, round height, ascender, descender, stem at mid x-height and letter gaps. Puts every value on the phi ladder of the wordmark stem with the chance rate, and notes half steps if the designer wants them. Runs golden_lint.py --svg on the same file and lists which of line/unit, gap/line, x-height/stem, icon height/x-height and part gap/stem are on, near or off, with the snap values. For an off relation it offers the value that would land or a logged departure with domain logo, the relation and a reason. It leaves optical corrections such as overshoot to the designer.
